title: Exploring the Côte de Nuits
description: A deep dive into Burgundy's red-wine heartland — its 9 principal villages, 24 Grands Crus, and the ultimate expression of Pinot Noir on this storied stretch of land.
lessons.0.title: Côte de Nuits Overview: Land of Red
lessons.0.slides.0.title: Côte de Nuits Overview: Land of Red
lessons.0.slides.0.subtitle: 15 minutes
lessons.0.slides.0.description: The Côte de Nuits is Burgundy's most prestigious red-wine zone, home to the great majority of its 24 Grands Crus. Stretching just 24 km from Marsannay to Nuits-Saint-Georges, this golden ribbon produces some of the world's most expensive and most refined Pinot Noir.
lessons.0.slides.1.title: 🗺️ Côte de Nuits Region Map
lessons.0.slides.2.title: Geography and Climate
lessons.0.slides.2.content: The Côte de Nuits lies south of Dijon and forms the northern half of the Côte d'Or. The region runs as a narrow north–south band only 300–400 m wide but 24 km long. East-facing slopes catch ample sunlight, and the warm-day, cool-night swing produces the elegance that defines Pinot Noir here.
lessons.0.slides.2.keyPoints.3: Microclimate: differs by village and even by parcel
lessons.0.slides.3.title: What Makes the Côte de Nuits Special
lessons.0.slides.3.content: Of Burgundy's 33 Grands Crus, 24 lie in the Côte de Nuits, mostly clustered between Gevrey-Chambertin and Vosne-Romanée. Limestone-dominated soils with varying marl content shape each village's distinctive style.
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.0: Grand Cru density: highest in the world
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.1: Soil diversity: from hard limestone to soft marl
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.2: Microclimate variations: sun, drainage and wind differ village by village
lessons.0.slides.3.keyPoints.3: Producer level: a roll-call of the world's elite domaines
lessons.0.slides.4.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.0.slides.4.points.0: 🍷 The Côte de Nuits is 93% red — Pinot Noir is the absolute lead role
lessons.0.slides.4.points.1: 🍷 Grands Crus are concentrated in the central section (Gevrey to Vosne-Romanée)
lessons.0.slides.4.points.2: 🍷 Village-level wines already show very high quality and are an excellent entry point

lessons.0.slides.6.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.0.question: Which type of wine is the Côte de Nuits best known for?
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.0.explanati: The Côte de Nuits is the world's heartland for top-tier Pinot Noir. The most legendary Grands Crus — Romanée-Conti, Chambertin, Musigny and so on — are concentrated along this 20 km north–south strip of slopes.
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.1.question: Which is the most famous, and northernmost, Grand Cru village of the Côte de Nuits?
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.1.explanati: Gevrey-Chambertin is the major Grand Cru village at the northern end of the Côte de Nuits. With more Grands Crus than almost any other Burgundy village (Chambertin, Mazis-Chambertin and others), it is famed for its powerful, concentrated style and serves as the gateway to the Côte de Nuits.
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.2.question: Which describe the standing of DRC (Domaine de la Romanée-Conti) in Burgundy? (multiple answers)
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.2.options.0: A. The most famous and most expensive estate in Burgundy
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.2.options.1: B. Sole owner of the entire Romanée-Conti Grand Cru (1.8 ha)
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.2.explanati: DRC is Burgundy's most legendary estate: it owns the Romanée-Conti Grand Cru in its entirety; it follows biodynamic and organic viticulture; and it makes both red and white wines (not whites only). Its bottles repeatedly set auction records around the world.
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.3.question: What makes the Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru most distinctive?
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.3.options.0: A. The entire Clos is vinified by a single winemaker
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.3.options.1: B. It is Burgundy's smallest Grand Cru
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.3.options.2: C. 50 ha shared by more than 80 different owners
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.3.options.3: D. It lies in Chablis and is the only mineral red
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.3.explanati: Clos de Vougeot is the extreme example of Burgundy's fragmented ownership: a 50 ha Grand Cru shared by more than 80 owners, with quality varying enormously from cellar to cellar — a fascinating case study of "terroir vs. winemaker".
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.4.question: What kind of rock dominates Côte de Nuits soils, and what does it bring to the wine?
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.4.options.0: A. Sandstone, contributing fresh fruit aromatics
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.4.options.2: C. A limestone-and-clay mix, lending complexity and ageing potential
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.4.options.3: D. Volcanic rock, giving a distinctive smoky character
lessons.0.slides.6.questions.4.explanati: The Côte de Nuits is built on a mix of limestone, clay and marl. This combination provides excellent drainage and gives Pinot Noir its fine-grained structure, stony minerality and capacity for long ageing.
lessons.0.slides.7.title: Summary
lessons.0.slides.7.content: The Côte de Nuits is Pinot Noir's paradise. Each village has its own personality — from powerful Gevrey to elegant Chambolle — for an enormous stylistic range, but all sharing the very highest quality.

lessons.1.slides.2.title: Marsannay: A Colourful Introduction
lessons.1.slides.2.content: Marsannay is the northernmost village of the Côte de Nuits and the only appellation permitted to bottle red, white and rosé. There are no Grands Crus, but Village and Premier Cru wines deliver excellent quality for the price.
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.1: Style: fresh, fruity, easy-drinking and approachable
lessons.1.slides.2.keyPoints.3: Best for: the ideal entry point to the Côte de Nuits
lessons.1.slides.3.title: Fixin: The Brother of Gevrey
lessons.1.slides.3.content: Fixin neighbours Gevrey-Chambertin, sharing similar soils and a comparable style at a more accessible price. Five Premiers Crus deliver firm, structured wines that need bottle age.
lessons.1.slides.3.keyPoints.0: Style: powerful, tightly structured, with prominent tannins
lessons.1.slides.4.title: Gevrey-Chambertin: King of the Côte de Nuits
lessons.1.slides.4.content: With nine Grands Crus, Gevrey-Chambertin is the largest and most celebrated village of the Côte de Nuits. The wines are powerful, complex and exceptionally long-lived — the benchmark of red Burgundy.
lessons.1.slides.5.title: 🏆 Chambertin & Clos de Bèze
lessons.1.slides.5.content:
**Chambertin** (12.9 ha)
Napoleon's favourite and the most powerful Grand Cru of the Côte de Nuits. Deep and complex with thick tannin, it reveals supreme elegance with age. Ageing potential: 10–30 years.

**Chambertin-Clos de Bèze** (15.4 ha)
Standing shoulder to shoulder with Chambertin, with slightly more elegance and an equally grand structure. Ageing potential: 10–30 years.
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.0: The two may use one another's name, but generally retain their own
lessons.1.slides.5.keyPoints.1: Clos de Bèze may be labelled Chambertin, but not the reverse
lessons.1.slides.6.title: 🏆 The Charmes Family of Grands Crus
lessons.1.slides.6.content:
**Charmes-Chambertin** (31.1 ha) — the largest Grand Cru.
Soft and seductive, comparatively approachable, the most accessible of Gevrey's Grands Crus. Ageing potential: 8–20 years.

**Mazoyères-Chambertin** (18.3 ha)
May be labelled Charmes-Chambertin; similar in style. Ageing potential: 8–20 years.
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.0: Charmes is the largest Grand Cru, with relatively higher production
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.1: Friendlier prices than the other Grands Crus: €100–300
lessons.1.slides.6.keyPoints.2: Perfect for a first taste of Gevrey at Grand Cru level
lessons.1.slides.7.title: 🏆 Other Fine Grands Crus (1/2)
lessons.1.slides.7.content:
**Chapelle-Chambertin** (5.4 ha)
Elegant and finely drawn, with delicate tannins. Ageing potential: 8–20 years.

**Griotte-Chambertin** (2.7 ha)
Small and refined, with morello-cherry (griotte) aromatics. Ageing potential: 8–20 years.
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.0: Smaller parcels often allow even sharper focus on quality
lessons.1.slides.7.keyPoints.1: Griotte is one of the very smallest Grands Crus by area
lessons.1.slides.8.title: 🏆 Other Fine Grands Crus (2/2)
lessons.1.slides.8.content:
**Latricières-Chambertin** (7.4 ha)
Fine and elegant, balanced between power and grace. Ageing potential: 8–20 years.

**Mazis-Chambertin** (9.1 ha)
Powerful and firmly built. Ageing potential: 10–25 years.

**Ruchottes-Chambertin** (3.3 ha)
A rare, tiny parcel with elegant minerality. Ageing potential: 8–20 years.
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.0: Mazis is stylistically closest to Chambertin
lessons.1.slides.8.keyPoints.1: Ruchottes sits highest on the slope, with marked minerality
lessons.1.slides.9.title: 💡 Key Take-aways
lessons.1.slides.9.points.0: 🍷 Gevrey-Chambertin Village wines are already high-quality; the Premiers Crus are exceptional
lessons.1.slides.9.points.1: 🍷 Chambertin and Clos de Bèze can use each other's names, but normally retain their own
lessons.1.slides.9.points.2: 🍷 Fixin is the value play — close to Gevrey in style at a much more friendly price

lessons.2.slides.2.title: Morey-Saint-Denis: The Quiet Gem
lessons.2.slides.2.content: Morey-Saint-Denis owns five Grands Crus but enjoys far less fame than its neighbours Gevrey and Chambolle. Its wines sit between the two — both powerful and elegant — making it a connoisseur's favourite.

lessons.2.slides.3.title: Chambolle-Musigny: Queen of the Côte de Nuits
lessons.2.slides.3.content: Chambolle-Musigny is famed for its "feminine" style — silken texture, abundant floral aromatics, fine-grained refinement. The Musigny Grand Cru is one of the most elegant wines of the Côte de Nuits.
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.0: Two Grands Crus: Musigny, and the principal portion of Bonnes-Mares
lessons.2.slides.3.keyPoints.1: Style: ultra-refined elegance, with violet and rose-petal aromatics

lessons.2.slides.4.title: Vougeot: A Witness to History
lessons.2.slides.4.content: Vougeot is famous for the Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru — at 50 ha, the largest Grand Cru in Burgundy, founded by Cistercian monks in the 12th century. Today over 80 owners share this historic vineyard.
lessons.2.slides.4.keyPoints.0: One Grand Cru: Clos de Vougeot (50.6 ha)
lessons.2.slides.4.keyPoints.1: Style: varies enormously with the parcel's location

lessons.2.slides.4.keyPoints.3: Bottom line: the producer matters more than the vineyard name

lessons.2.slides.5.points.0: 🍷 Morey-Saint-Denis offers superb value and is well worth deeper exploration

lessons.2.slides.5.points.2: 🍷 Clos de Vougeot varies hugely by parcel — the producer matters more than the vineyard name

lessons.3.slides.10.questions.3.question: What makes Clos de Vougeot most distinctive?
C. 50 ha shared by more than 80 owners
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.3.explanat: Clos de Vougeot is the extreme example of Burgundy's fragmented ownership.
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.4.question: What rock dominates Côte de Nuits soils?
C. Limestone-clay mix, lending complexity and ageing potential
lessons.3.slides.10.questions.4.explanat: A mix of limestone, clay and marl gives Pinot Noir its structure, minerality and ageing capacity.
lessons.3.slides.11.title: Summary
lessons.3.slides.11.content: Vosne-Romanée delivers the ultimate expression of Pinot Noir, the very pinnacle of Burgundy. Nuits-Saint-Georges, lacking a Grand Cru, nonetheless produces outstanding Premiers Crus at outstanding value.
